chunks: As for what Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā narrated from al-ʿAmrakī, from ʿAlī ibn Jaʿfar, from his brother Mūsā ibn Jaʿfar عليه السلام: I asked him about a man whose garment fell upon a dead dog. He said:
He should sprinkle it with water and pray in it; there is no harm.

So this report clarifies that the ruling regarding the dog, whether dead or alive, is the same concerning sprinkling water on the garment that touched it when it was dry. And the first report is to be taken as specific to the body of the human being, so there is no contradiction between them in any way.

key_terms.الْخَبَرُ: The report or hadith being used as evidence.
key_terms.الْكَلْبِ: The dog, whose contact is the subject of the ruling.
key_terms.بِالْمَاءِ: With water, used here for purifying by sprinkling.
key_terms.جَافًّا: Dry, indicating the condition affecting the legal ruling.
key_terms.مَيِّتًا: Dead, describing the dog's state in the ruling.
key_terms.يَنْضِحُهُ: He sprinkles water upon it lightly.

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a garment touches a dead dog while dry?
ai.summary: This hadith states that if a dry garment touches a dead dog, it is sufficient to sprinkle water on it and one may pray in it. The accompanying explanation clarifies that the ruling for a dog, dead or alive, is the same in this dry-contact case, and that another report is restricted to the human corpse, thereby removing contradiction between the narrations.
